https://www.theqicollective.com.au/.body_text: The Qi Collective | Acupuncture & Chinese Medicine Adelaide The Qi Collective Balanced + Integrated Healing Qi is the vital energy that flows through all living things — the quiet current that connects body, mind and spirit. In Chinese medicine, Qi is the force that moves, nourishes and sustains us, creating harmony when it flows freely. It is breath. It is movement. It is life. At its heart, Qi is the art of returning to balance — allowing the body to soften, restore and reconnect with its innate capacity to heal. WELCOME TO THE QI COLLECTIVE Located in Rose Park, Adelaide, The Qi Collective brings together a team of multidisciplinary practitioners who are committed to creating a space for you to rest, heal, learn, grow and understand yourself and your innate health and wellbeing on a deeper level. Our Practitioners work on the basis that understanding true health and wellbeing means understanding and addressing all aspects of the human being and will work with you to connect the dots, understand yourself on a deeper level and move forward to a more balanced, healthier state. OUR MISSION Qi pronounced “chi” At The Qi Collective, our mission is to provide a clear, calm and high-vibrational wellness space, with exceptional practitioners who are deeply passionate about holistic wellbeing and guiding their clients on their healing journey. Services Traditional healing practices to support your health and wellbeing. Acupuncture Fine needles are placed at specific points to restore the flow of Qi, promoting natural healing and balance throughout the body. Herbal Medicine Customised herbal formulas and Chinese dietary advice to complement your treatment and support long-term wellness. Cupping Therapy Glass cups create suction to move stagnant blood, release tension, and remove toxins from muscles for relief from chronic pain. Cosmetic Acupuncture Natural facial rejuvenation using fine needles to stimulate collagen, improve circulation, and reduce fine lines for a refreshed appearance. Movement Classes Guided Qigong classes combine breath, gentle movement and mindful awareness to support steadiness, mobility and a deeper connection with your body. Workshops Small-group workshops offer practical learning in Chinese medicine, seasonal wellbeing and everyday self-care within a warm, supportive setting. Areas of Special Interest Women's Health Supporting hormonal balance, menstrual health, and overall wellbeing. Mental & Emotional Gentle support for anxiety, stress, and emotional wellness. Paediatrics Gentle treatments adapted for the unique needs of children. Peri-Natal Care From pre-conception through pregnancy to postpartum support. Pain Management Individualised support for persistent pain, muscular tension and day-to-day mobility. Chronic Health Conditions Whole-person care for ongoing concerns, including digestive issues and fatigue.

https://www.theqicollective.com.au/about.body_text: About Us | The Qi Collective The Qi Collective Balanced + Integrated Healing About The Qi Collective A space where you can arrive exactly as you are About us A community grounded in whole-person care The Qi Collective was founded by acupuncturist and energy healer Charlotte Powell, who envisioned a space that would bring together a community of like-minded practitioners with a deep connection and understanding of not only the physical, but the emotional and spiritual aspects of a person. A space where clients could arrive exactly as they are, and leave with a deeper sense of calm, balance and understanding of themselves and their journey. The meaning of Qi Qi pronounced “chi” The word Qi means ‘life force energy’. Qi is the vital energy that flows through all living things — the quiet current that connects body, mind and spirit. In Chinese medicine, Qi is the force that moves, nourishes and sustains us, creating harmony when it flows freely. It is breath. It is movement. It is life. At its heart, Qi is the art of returning to balance — allowing the body to soften, restore and reconnect with its innate capacity to heal. Our mission At The Qi Collective, our mission is to provide a clear, calm and high-vibrational wellness space, with exceptional practitioners who are deeply passionate about holistic wellbeing and guiding their clients on their healing journey. Our vision We imagine a world where preventative health care is the norm, where we honour our body, mind and spirit and caring for thyself is second nature for all. We endeavour to create an open, peaceful, empathetic and deeply nurturing space where you feel seen, heard and understood. Where we can work with you to help you understand your health, your body, and yourself on a deeper level. Meet our Practitioners

Women’s Health Endometriosis Menopause Digestive Health Shiatsu View full profile → ← All practitioners Charlotte Powell Classical Chinese Medicine Practitioner / Acupuncturist / Universal Healing (Reiki) Practitioner Charlotte is a degree-qualified and AHPRA registered Doctor of Chinese Medicine and Universal Healing (Reiki) Practitioner. Charlotte follows a holistic and open-minded approach to health and wellness, bringing awareness and focus to all aspects of the human being (physical, mental/emotional and spiritual). She acknowledges and understands the connection between these elements and ensures treatments work through the different layers to bring harmony back to the system. Charlotte has developed a deep love and passion for holistic health and wellbeing throughout her life, recognising throughout her own health journey how the integration of different holistic therapies can assist in creating an optimally healthy and balanced state of being. Deeply committed to assisting others on their health and wellbeing journey, Charlotte thrives in helping others find a deeper understanding of themselves and the world around them whilst inspiring them to commit to themselves and prioritise their own healing. Throughout her studies and years in practice, Charlotte has developed a special interest in treating Women’s Health conditions, Mental/Emotional/Spiritual wellbeing, Paediatrics and has developed her skills further in the Peri-Natal field caring for women from pre-conception through to postpartum and beyond. Charlotte has recently completed further study in Chinese Herbal Medicine and integrates this in her treatments where necessary. She is registered with AHPRA (Australian Health Practitioners Regulation Agency), is a fully accredited member of the Australian Acupuncture and Chinese Medicine Association (AACMA) and is a registered practitioner with the Chinese Medicine Board of Australia (CMBA). AHPRA Registered AACMA Member CMBA Registered Private health rebates may be available; please check with your health fund. ← All practitioners ← All practitioners Annabelle Boehm Classical Chinese Medicine Practitioner / Acupuncturist / Reiki Practitioner Annabelle is a Classical Chinese Medicine Practitioner, Acupuncturist, and Reiki Practitioner who supports people in reconnecting with their bodies and returning to a greater sense of balance. She works with a wide range of health concerns and has a particular interest in helping people navigate the emotional and mental barriers that can impact wellbeing. She understands that stress, overwhelm, anxiety, fear, burnout and unresolved life experiences can affect not only our emotional health but also our physical being and our ability to thrive. Her approach combines hands-on techniques, acupuncture, and energy work, tailored to each person. Annabelle has completed advanced training with Ann Cecil-Sterman and has studied the full 68-channel system of Classical Acupuncture, allowing her to work with a broad range of complex and chronic conditions. Annabelle supports people with: Hormonal and reproductive health, including fertility, pregnancy, menopause, and menstrual concerns Digestive issues and systemic inflammation Pain and musculoskeletal conditions Stress, burnout, anxiety, and nervous system dysregulation Autoimmune, complex and chronic health conditions Those who feel “off” despite normal test results At the heart of her practice is the intention to create a warm, safe, and supportive environment, where people feel heard, understood and empowered. Annabelle provides gentle, compassionate care as she guides her patients towards a greater sense of clarity, resilience, balance and wellbeing. AHPRA Registered AACMA Member CMBA Registered Private health rebates may be available; please check with your health fund. ← All practitioners ← All practitioners Kate O'Leary Classical Chinese Medicine Practitioner / Acupuncturist / Reiki Practitioner / Yoga Facilitator Kate is a degree-qualified Chinese Medicine Practitioner and Acupuncturist with a clinical approach strongly influenced by the principles of Classical Acupuncture. Her treatment philosophy is informed by an appreciation of the traditional foundations of Chinese Medicine, combined with an evidence-informed, patient-centred approach to care. Kate is Reiki attuned and offers energy work in addition to her acupuncture treatments. Before entering healthcare, Kate worked professionally in the arts, an experience that fostered creativity, observation and a deep understanding of the human experience. She has also maintained a dedicated yoga practice for more than 20 years and is a Yoga Facilitator with over 500 hours of registered teacher training, as well as an Ayurvedic Lifestyle Consultant. These complementary disciplines enhance her holistic approach to supporting health and wellbeing. Kate believes food is a central pillar of wellness and offers stand-alone Oriental Medicine Nutrition consultations. Kate has a particular interest in women’s health, with a focus on menopause, fertility, pregnancy and postpartum care. Her passion for supporting women during the perinatal period was inspired by her own experiences through pregnancy and birth with her two daughters. She teaches regular Pregnancy Yoga classes and birth preparation workshops. In addition, Kate offers postnatal home visits to assist in nourishing and supporting new mothers. She also enjoys working with patients experiencing autoimmune conditions, digestive disorders and chronic health concerns. Recognising the close relationship between physical and mental health, Kate places emotional wellbeing at the centre of her treatment approach. She is committed to providing personalised, comprehensive care that addresses the underlying patterns contributing to illness, rather than simply managing symptoms, helping patients achieve sustainable improvements in their health and quality of life. AHPRA Registered AACMA Member CMBA Registered Private health rebates may be available; please check with your health fund. ← All practitioners ← All practitioners Emily Floreani Chinese Medicine Practitioner / Acupuncturist / Yoga Teacher Emily is a deeply passionate acupuncturist and yoga teacher who loves natural healing. She was introduced to complementary medicine from a young age and now loves to support others on their healing journey. One of Emily’s core beliefs is that the body is powerful and that, as human beings, we have the capacity within us to heal — sometimes we just need a hand along the way. It is through this idea that Emily practises: we are smart, intelligent beings who can become unbalanced through lifestyle stressors or traumatic experiences. Emily utilises Traditional Chinese Medicine and Reiki in her practice. Through her knowledge of these medicines, her purpose is to create an environment where you feel safe to heal, grow and thrive in life. Guided by her own experiences with acupuncture, Emily is passionate about helping others feel their best in their body — physically, mentally and emotionally. Some of Emily’s areas of expertise include: Menstrual cycle balancing for teenage girls Women’s health concerns Feelings of stress and overwhelm Regulation of the nervous system Digestive concerns AHPRA Registered AACMA Member CMBA Registered Private health rebates may be available; please check with your health fund. ← All practitioners ← All practitioners Prue Klausener Chinese Medicine Practitioner / Acupuncturist / Shiatsu Practitioner / Yoga Teacher Prue is a degree-qualified Chinese Medicine Practitioner and Acupuncturist, with a diploma in Shiatsu and Oriental Therapies. Strongly influenced by the Zen approach she was introduced to during her initial studies in Chinese medicine and Shiatsu, Prue believes that healing can be accessed through the body’s internal networks and acupuncture channels, and draws upon a combination of her skills to help facilitate this process. Prue has practised and taught Hatha Yoga for almost two decades, integrating over time her experience in meditation and eastern healing traditions. She has travelled extensively throughout the East, spending extended periods in India, Nepal and Thailand, where she deepened her understanding of Yoga practice and philosophy, Buddhism and Taoism. In 2025, Prue spent three months with her family volunteering in a rural health clinic in Nepal, an experience that offered a profound sense of immersion, connection and perspective. A mother to two daughters, and a devoted partner, daughter and friend, Prue has connections across the world and takes pride in the many cultures that make up the fabric of her family and friendships. She lived for almost a decade in Switzerland where she learnt to speak Italian, an accomplishment that came through many years of openness, cultural adaptivity and persistence. A culmination of her life and health experiences, spiritual nature, fascination with the body and love of human connection have shaped Prue into the practitioner she is today. Prue has a special interest in women’s health, particularly Endometriosis and Menopause, as well as digestive health and emotional well being. She is committed to ongoing study, and both personal and professional development, continually deepening her knowledge and skills so that her patients receive thoughtful, individualised support throughout their healing journey. Prue offers Chinese Medicine consultations with Japanese-influenced and classical Acupuncture, as well as combined Acupuncture and Shiatsu treatments. Her approach brings together the therapeutic benefits of Acupuncture with the grounding, hands-on nature of Shiatsu, creating a deeply restorative treatment experience that considers the whole person. https://www.theqicollective.com.au/servi.body_text: Services | The Qi Collective The Qi Collective Balanced + Integrated Healing Our Services Traditional healing practices to support your health and wellbeing Acupuncture Acupuncture is a practice of TCM and involves the insertion of fine needles into specific points on the skin, located at various locations around the body. The points chosen are specific to the receiver and the underlying pattern being treated. Acu-points are found along meridians (channels of vital energy flow) throughout the body. The meridians are all interconnected and also connect our external to our internal organs, joints, sinews, tendons etc. Acupuncture works to re-establish flow and balance within the body, removing blockages, tonifying deficiencies and reducing excesses to assist the receiver's overall state of well-being. Acupuncture may assist with conditions such as: Women's health / Men's health Digestive issues Mental health Insomnia Respiratory issues Skin conditions Hay fever / allergies Pregnancy Fertility Paediatrics And more Cupping Cupping sessions can be booked as stand-alone or cupping may be included within an acupuncture session. Cupping involves the use of glass cups which suction the skin and muscle inwards to move stagnant blood and draw toxins from the tissue and muscles. It activates the flow of Qi and Blood through the sinew channels (muscles) to assist in treating pain, stiffness, and many other health issues. Cupping may create circular marks on the skin that range from pale pink to dark purple; this provides us with an explanation of underlying pathology. Although marks can sometimes look quite dark, cupping should never be painful. Your practitioner will ensure you are comfortable and relaxed throughout the treatment. Chinese Herbal Medicine Individualised herbal formulas are prescribed to support your health goals and complement acupuncture treatment. Chinese Dietetics Personalised food guidance grounded in Chinese medicine helps you nourish your body according to your constitution and needs. Cosmetic Acupuncture In a cosmetic acupuncture session, fine needles are placed along the face and into facial muscles to improve the appearance of fine lines, wrinkles, sagging skin and bags under the eyes. The insertion of the needles stimulates the release of collagen and encourages circulation of blood and Qi to the area, which may create a more plump, bright and fresh appearance to the skin. Body support points may also be incorporated to treat skin concerns as well as facial Gua Sha, Tui Na (Massage), and other techniques tailored individually and discussed prior to treatment. Pediatric Acupuncture Paediatric sessions involve a combination of Acupuncture (tiny needles for children), Acupressure, Moxibustion, Tui Na (Chinese massage) and Reiki (if both you and your child consent) to assist in bringing the body back into balance. If a child is afraid of needles—no worries, specific acupressure tools can work with equal effect to needles. Paediatric acupuncture may assist with issues such as: Digestive issues Sleep disturbances Hyperactivity / ADHD Bed-wetting Growth delays Physical pain / ailments Asthma Skin issues Recurrent colds / viruses And more Reiki/Universal Healing Reiki is a form of energetic healing that works with the body's main energy centres (chakras) and the aura. The body's chakras process energetic vibrations between the outer world and the physical body and soul. When balanced, energy can flow freely through the chakras, harmonising the mind, body and spirit. When chakras are blocked, imbalances can cause mental, physical, emotional and spiritual ailments. During a Reiki session, universal source Qi/energy is channelled via the practitioner to the receiver using both hands-on and hands-off techniques. The energy is specific to the receiver and always works to bring the body back into balance by resolving blockages, clearing away negativity and establishing free flow of energy throughout the chakra and subtle energy bodies. Reiki is an extremely relaxing therapy and may provide the receiver with a sense of clarity, calm and an overall 'light' feeling. Intuitive guidance or information may be offered to the receiver throughout these sessions if the receiver is open. Movement Classes Our Qigong classes bring together gentle movement, breath and focused awareness. Sessions are designed to be approachable and offer time to slow down, reconnect with your body and cultivate a steadier sense of energy and balance. Workshops Our workshops create space for shared learning around Chinese medicine, seasonal wellbeing and practical self-care. Each session combines accessible guidance with tools you can carry into daily life, with topics and dates announced as scheduled. Ready to Begin?
